description: JVM bytes ops/identity slice (jvm-v12-int32-bytes D3/D4; the BackendConformanceTest passing pins the lane contract names): the v1.2 bytes core on the retained JVM backend — bytes(length) lowers to a fresh zero-filled $DealRt.Bytes wrapper, b.length is the immutable signed-int32 logical allocation length, reads yield the unsigned 0..255 byte, a write mutates exactly one byte and returns the written value, reference-copy assignment/aliasing with reference identity equality (alias ===, distinct buffers !==, nullable-vs-null), E8012 for negative allocation length and out-of-bounds indexes (bytes never append), E8013 for values outside 0..255 after the receiver/index/RHS all evaluated, failed writes changing no storage, and the empty buffer. Every case runs the real frontend (lexer → parser → name resolver → type checker) under the A5 per-case invocation (COMMON_SHADOW + DEAL_V1_2_INT32 — no case is catalogued as legacy-dependent) → real JvmBackend codegen → javac → java executing the emitted artifact; a bypassed codegen or JVM execution produces no output and fails the fixture. Result-value assertions are JVM-only (the runner prints the test export's return value).

tests.name: jvm-bytes-zero-fill-alloc
tests.description: v1.2 bytes: bytes(4) allocates a fresh buffer whose four bytes all read 0 and whose length is the immutable signed-int32 allocation length 4

tests.name: jvm-bytes-unsigned-roundtrip
tests.description: v1.2 bytes: writes of 255, 128, and 0 store exactly those bytes and reads yield the unsigned 0..255 values (255 + 128 + 0 = 383)

tests.name: jvm-bytes-write-returns-value
tests.description: v1.2 bytes: an expression-position write returns the written unsigned value (200)

tests.name: jvm-bytes-write-exactly-one-byte
tests.description: v1.2 bytes: a successful write mutates exactly one byte — writing 7 at index 2 leaves the other three bytes at zero

tests.name: jvm-bytes-immutable-length
tests.description: v1.2 bytes: b.length reads the immutable logical allocation length as int through an alias, and bytes(0) allocates a zero-length buffer (3 - 3 + 0 = 0)

tests.name: jvm-bytes-length-int-arithmetic
tests.description: v1.2 bytes: the compiler-resolved b.length is a signed-int32 int operand — a length read of 3 computes 3 * 2 + 1 = 7 through int arithmetic

tests.name: jvm-bytes-alias-mutation
tests.description: v1.2 bytes: assignment copies the reference — alias[2] = 7 is visible through the original binding b as b[2] === 7

tests.name: jvm-bytes-identity-alias-eq
tests.description: v1.2 bytes: equality is reference identity — a reference copy of the same allocation compares equal

tests.name: jvm-bytes-identity-distinct-ne
tests.description: v1.2 bytes: two fresh allocations of the same length are distinct references — === is false and !== is true

tests.name: jvm-bytes-identity-nullable-null
tests.description: v1.2 bytes: nullable-vs-null reference equality in both directions — a null bytes | null binding equals null, a non-null value does not, and null === nothing holds on the right

tests.name: jvm-bytes-fresh-instances
tests.description: v1.2 bytes: two fresh allocations own independent storage — writing 9 into the first leaves the second's byte at zero

tests.name: jvm-bytes-fn-param-return
tests.description: v1.2 bytes: buffers flow through function parameters and returns by reference — fill writes 200 into the shared allocation, the caller reads it back (200 + 3 = 203)

tests.name: jvm-bytes-negative-length-e8012
tests.description: v1.2 bytes: bytes(-1) raises E8012 (the negative allocation length) before any object is published

tests.name: jvm-bytes-read-bounds-high-e8012
tests.description: v1.2 bytes: a read at the index equal to the length (b[4] on a 4-byte buffer) is out of bounds and raises E8012

tests.name: jvm-bytes-read-bounds-low-e8012
tests.description: v1.2 bytes: a negative index read (b[-1]) is out of bounds and raises E8012

tests.name: jvm-bytes-write-bounds-high-e8012
tests.description: v1.2 bytes: a write at the index equal to the length (b[2] on a 2-byte buffer) is out of bounds and raises E8012 — bytes writes never append

tests.name: jvm-bytes-write-bounds-low-e8012
tests.description: v1.2 bytes: a negative index write (b[-1] = 7) is out of bounds and raises E8012

tests.name: jvm-bytes-empty-read-e8012
tests.description: v1.2 bytes: reading b[0] of a bytes(0) empty buffer is out of bounds and raises E8012

tests.name: jvm-bytes-empty-write-e8012
tests.description: v1.2 bytes: writing b[0] = 1 on a bytes(0) empty buffer is out of bounds and raises E8012 (never an append)

tests.name: jvm-bytes-write-value-high-e8013
tests.description: v1.2 bytes: writing 256 (above the unsigned byte range) raises E8013

tests.name: jvm-bytes-write-value-low-e8013
tests.description: v1.2 bytes: writing -1 (below the unsigned byte range) raises E8013

tests.name: jvm-bytes-eval-order-single
tests.description: v1.2 bytes: a write evaluates the receiver, the index, and the RHS exactly once each and strictly left to right — pick records 1, the index records 2, the RHS records 3, and the value lands at buf[2]

tests.name: jvm-bytes-write-validation-after-rhs
tests.description: v1.2 bytes: write validation runs only after every operand completed — the receiver (1), index (2), and a side-effecting RHS (3) all record before the RHS's out-of-range 300 raises E8013, and the failed write changes no storage (buf[1] stays zero)
